datadog_ai_custom_rule_response: `datadog_ai_custom_rule_response` is a custom detection rule for Datadog's AI/LLM observability surface -- a condition written against LLM Observability trace data (prompts, completions, tool calls) that flags a real problem, like a policy violation or a quality regression, as traces flow through a monitored application.
datadog_ai_custom_rule_revision_response: `datadog_ai_custom_rule_revision_response` is one saved, versioned revision of an `datadog_ai_custom_rule_response` -- the rule's own real edit history, letting a team roll a custom AI detection rule back to a prior version or see exactly what changed and when.
datadog_ai_custom_ruleset_response: `datadog_ai_custom_ruleset_response` is a named collection of `datadog_ai_custom_rule_response` rules grouped together and applied as one unit to LLM Observability traces -- the organizing container a team attaches to an LLM application rather than managing individual rules ad hoc.
datadog_api_key_response: `datadog_api_key_response` is the credential the Datadog Agent uses to submit metrics, traces, and events to your organization -- every agent-based integration authenticates with one. It's organization-specific, not tied to any one user, and is the primary way infrastructure data actually gets into Datadog in the first place.
datadog_apikey_response: `datadog_apikey_response` is a real Datadog organization API key -- the credential the Datadog Agent and integrations use to submit metrics, traces, and logs. Distinct from `datadog_api_key_response` (v1): this is v2's own richer representation of the identical real concept, with `datadog_partial_application_key_response` and `datadog_application_key_response` as its companion credential.
datadog_application_key_response: `datadog_application_key_response` works alongside an API key to authorize programmatic access to Datadog's own API. Unlike an API key, an application key is tied to the user who created it and carries that user's own permissions -- it's what a script or integration uses to act on Datadog data on that user's behalf, not what an agent uses to submit it.
datadog_application_security_policy_resp: `datadog_application_security_policy_response` is a policy governing Datadog Application Security Management (ASM) behavior for a service -- which protections (in-app WAF, threat detection) are active and how ASM should respond when it detects an attack.
datadog_application_security_waf_custom_: `datadog_application_security_waf_custom_rule_response` is a custom Web Application Firewall rule under Datadog ASM -- a condition an organization writes itself (beyond Datadog's own managed rule set) to detect or block a specific real attack pattern against a protected application.
datadog_application_security_waf_exclusi: `datadog_application_security_waf_exclusion_filter_response` is a real, scoped exception that tells Datadog ASM's WAF to skip evaluating specific traffic (a known-safe path, a trusted source) that would otherwise trigger a false positive.
datadog_arbitrary_rule_response: `datadog_arbitrary_rule_response` represents a real, user-defined logic rule under Datadog's Cloud Security Management custom-rule framework -- a condition expressed against cloud resource configuration or activity that doesn't fit one of Datadog's own pre-built detection categories.
datadog_auth_nmapping_response: `datadog_auth_nmapping_response` is a real authentication-to-identity mapping used by Datadog's own auth-n integration layer -- associating an external identity (from an upstream auth provider) with the internal principal Datadog authorization decisions are made against.
datadog_automation_rule_response: `datadog_automation_rule_response` is a real Datadog Case Management automation rule -- a trigger condition (a new case matching certain criteria) paired with an action (assign, tag, notify) that runs automatically so a security or ops team doesn't have to triage every case by hand.
datadog_aws_cur_config_response: `datadog_aws_cur_config_response` is Datadog's own configured connection to an AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) -- which S3 bucket and report Datadog reads to power real, granular AWS cost visibility inside Cloud Cost Management, beyond what the base AWS integration's billing estimate alone provides.
datadog_aws_on_demand_response: `datadog_aws_on_demand_response` represents a real, on-demand (as opposed to continuously scheduled) scan or check Datadog Cloud Security Management runs against an AWS account -- used to get fresh posture/vulnerability results outside the normal periodic scan cadence.
datadog_aws_scan_options_response: `datadog_aws_scan_options_response` is the real, configured scan settings Datadog Cloud Security Management uses for a connected AWS account -- what gets scanned (resource types, regions) and how often, controlling the actual scope of AWS posture and vulnerability coverage.
datadog_awsaccount_response: `datadog_awsaccount_response` is a real AWS account connected to Datadog's own AWS integration -- the account ID, IAM role Datadog assumes, and which AWS namespaces/services are enabled for metric collection from that specific account.
datadog_awscloud_auth_persona_mapping_re: `datadog_awscloud_auth_persona_mapping_response` is a real mapping between an AWS IAM identity and a Datadog Cloud Security persona/role -- part of Datadog's cloud-native, keyless AWS authentication model, associating cloud-side identities with the access level Datadog grants them.
datadog_azure_scan_options: `datadog_azure_scan_options` is the Azure counterpart to `datadog_aws_scan_options_response` -- the real, configured scope and cadence Datadog Cloud Security Management uses when scanning a connected Azure subscription for posture and vulnerability findings.
datadog_budget_with_entries: `datadog_budget_with_entries` is a real Datadog Cloud Cost Management budget -- a spend target broken down by real budget entries (per team, per time period), used to track actual cloud spend against a plan and alert when a team is trending over budget.
datadog_campaign_response: `datadog_campaign_response` is a real, structured initiative inside Datadog's Security Inbox / vulnerability remediation workflow -- a grouped set of findings assigned to a team with a real, tracked goal (fix these vulnerabilities by this date), not an individual finding itself.
datadog_case_response: `datadog_case_response` is a real case inside Datadog Case Management -- a trackable unit of work (a security incident, an operational issue) with real status, assignee, priority, and linked evidence, the same real primitive that powers Datadog's own Cloud SIEM and App Security investigation workflows.
datadog_case_view_response: `datadog_case_view_response` is a saved, filtered view over Datadog Case Management cases -- a real, named query (by status, team, priority) a user or team saves to quickly get back to the specific slice of cases they work from day to day.
datadog_change_request_response: `datadog_change_request_response` is a real, tracked change request under Datadog's change-management surface -- a proposed infrastructure or configuration change with its own approval workflow, letting teams correlate incidents against what actually changed and when.
datadog_cloud_workload_security_agent_po: `datadog_cloud_workload_security_agent_policy_response` is a real policy controlling what Datadog Cloud Workload Security (CWS) monitors and enforces on a protected host or container -- which detection rules are active and in what mode (detect-only vs. block).
datadog_cloud_workload_security_agent_ru: `datadog_cloud_workload_security_agent_rule_response` is one real detection rule evaluated by the Datadog Agent's CWS module directly on a host -- a condition over real kernel-level events (file access, process execution, network activity) that flags or blocks a runtime threat.
datadog_cloudflare_account_response: `datadog_cloudflare_account_response` is a real Cloudflare account connected to Datadog's own Cloudflare integration -- the credentials and account identifier Datadog uses to pull Cloudflare's own metrics and logs (CDN, WAF, DNS) into Datadog.
datadog_confluent_account_response: `datadog_confluent_account_response` is a real Confluent Cloud account connected to Datadog's Confluent Cloud integration -- the credentials Datadog uses to collect Kafka cluster metrics and logs from that account.
datadog_confluent_resource_response: `datadog_confluent_resource_response` is one real Confluent Cloud resource (a Kafka cluster, connector, or similar) Datadog has discovered and is monitoring under a connected `datadog_confluent_account_response`.
datadog_custom_destination_response: `datadog_custom_destination_response` is a real, configured forwarding destination for Datadog Log Forwarding -- an external endpoint (Splunk HEC, a generic HTTP endpoint, cloud storage) logs matching a filter get re-forwarded to, alongside Datadog's own log pipeline.
datadog_custom_rule_response: `datadog_custom_rule_response` is a real, general-purpose custom detection rule -- a user-authored condition used across one of Datadog's security or observability products where the built-in rule library doesn't already cover a team's own specific requirement.
datadog_custom_ruleset_response: `datadog_custom_ruleset_response` is a named collection of `datadog_custom_rule_response` rules applied together, the general-purpose counterpart to the more specific `datadog_ai_custom_ruleset_response` and `datadog_sast_ruleset_response`.
datadog_dashboard: `datadog_dashboard` is a real-time visualization built from Datadog's own metrics, traces, and logs, used to track KPIs, spot anomalies, and troubleshoot problems as they happen. Dashboards come in a few real layout styles -- grid-based, timeboard, and free-form screenboard -- suited to different jobs, from an always-on status view to ad hoc data exploration.
datadog_dashboard_list: `datadog_dashboard_list` is a named collection used to organize dashboards so a team can search, browse, and share a related set of them instead of hunting through every dashboard in the organization individually.
datadog_dataset_response_single: `datadog_dataset_response_single` is one real, defined dataset within Datadog's data platform -- a named, scoped view over log or event data (by index, query, or source) that other Datadog features (like security monitoring rules) can be scoped to run against.
datadog_datastore: `datadog_datastore` is a real, structured key-value data store inside Datadog Workflow Automation and App Builder -- a place workflows and custom apps read and write real, persistent data (a lookup table, a small state store) without needing an external database.
datadog_degradation: `datadog_degradation` is a real, detected performance degradation tracked by Datadog -- a specific service or endpoint whose latency, error rate, or other health signal has measurably worsened, surfaced as its own trackable entity rather than buried in a raw metric.
datadog_degradation_template: `datadog_degradation_template` is a reusable template defining how Datadog detects and reports a `datadog_degradation` -- the real thresholds and signals a team configures once and applies across many services rather than hand-tuning detection per service.
datadog_deployment_gate_response: `datadog_deployment_gate_response` is a real Datadog Deployment Gate -- an automated check (based on real monitors, SLOs, or error rates) wired into a CI/CD pipeline that blocks or allows a deployment from proceeding based on live service health.
datadog_deployment_gates_evaluation_resu: `datadog_deployment_gates_evaluation_result_response` is the real, recorded outcome of one `datadog_deployment_gate_response` evaluation -- whether the gate passed or failed for a specific deployment, and the underlying health data that decision was based on.
datadog_deployment_rule_response: `datadog_deployment_rule_response` is a real rule governing Datadog's deployment tracking -- how Datadog Deployment Visibility identifies and correlates a deployment event from CI/CD data with the services and infrastructure it affects.
datadog_doradeployment_fetch_response: `datadog_doradeployment_fetch_response` is a real, queried set of DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) deployment-frequency metrics -- one of the four real DORA metrics Datadog computes from an organization's own CI/CD and deployment data to measure engineering delivery performance.
datadog_dorafailure_fetch_response: `datadog_dorafailure_fetch_response` is the real, queried change-failure-rate half of Datadog's DORA metrics -- how often a deployment led to a real incident or rollback, computed alongside `datadog_doradeployment_fetch_response`'s own deployment-frequency data.
datadog_downtime: `datadog_downtime` schedules a window where monitor alerts and notifications are silenced without stopping the monitors themselves from evaluating or changing state. It's the real mechanism for suppressing noise during planned maintenance or a deployment, filterable by specific monitors or by tag, and supports both one-time and recurring schedules.
datadog_downtime_response: `datadog_downtime_response` is v2's own richer representation of a Datadog downtime -- a real, scheduled suppression window that mutes monitor alerts for a specific scope (a host, a service, a tag) during planned maintenance, so expected changes don't page anyone.
datadog_due_date_rule_response: `datadog_due_date_rule_response` is a real rule that automatically assigns a due date to a Datadog Case Management case or Security Inbox finding based on its own severity or type -- the mechanism behind Datadog's real SLA tracking for security and operational work.
datadog_entity_integration_config_respon: `datadog_entity_integration_config_response` is real, per-entity configuration for how Datadog's Software Catalog links a service, or other cataloged entity, to an external integration (a repository, a dashboard, an on-call schedule) it references.
datadog_environment_response: `datadog_environment_response` is a real, named environment (production, staging, and similar) as modeled by Datadog's App Builder/Software Catalog surface -- a real deployment target an app or service is associated with, distinct from the free-form `env` tag used elsewhere in Datadog.
datadog_escalation_policy: `datadog_escalation_policy` is a real Datadog On-Call escalation policy -- the ordered chain of who gets notified, and after how long the alert escalates to the next person or team, if a page for an active incident goes unacknowledged.
datadog_event_response: `datadog_event_response` represents one entry in Datadog's own event stream -- generated automatically by monitors, Error Tracking, and over a hundred real integrations (Kubernetes, Jenkins, and similar), or submitted directly. Events get correlated together to cut down alert fatigue and feed the Triage Inbox teams use to investigate and resolve incidents.
datadog_execution_policy_response: `datadog_execution_policy_response` is a real policy governing how a Datadog Workflow Automation workflow is allowed to run -- real constraints like which connections/credentials it may use and under what conditions, enforced by Datadog before a workflow executes.
datadog_fastly_account_response: `datadog_fastly_account_response` is a real Fastly account connected to Datadog's own Fastly integration -- the credentials Datadog uses to pull Fastly CDN metrics and logs into Datadog.
datadog_fastly_service_response: `datadog_fastly_service_response` is one real Fastly service Datadog has discovered and is monitoring under a connected `datadog_fastly_account_response`.
datadog_feature_flag_response: `datadog_feature_flag_response` is a real feature flag as tracked by Datadog's own feature-flag correlation surface -- letting a team see a flag's real rollout state alongside the metrics, traces, and errors it may be causing.
datadog_form_response: `datadog_form_response` is a real, structured form definition used inside Datadog Workflow Automation and App Builder -- the real fields, layout, and validation a user-facing intake form (used to kick off a workflow or gather structured input) is built from.
datadog_gcp_scan_options: `datadog_gcp_scan_options` is the GCP counterpart to `datadog_aws_scan_options_response`/`datadog_azure_scan_options` -- the real, configured scope and cadence Datadog Cloud Security Management uses when scanning a connected Google Cloud project.
datadog_gcp_uc_config_response: `datadog_gcp_uc_config_response` is Datadog's own configured connection to Google Cloud's Usage/Cost data export -- the GCP counterpart to `datadog_aws_cur_config_response`, powering granular GCP cost visibility inside Cloud Cost Management.
datadog_get_action_connection_response: `datadog_get_action_connection_response` is a real, configured connection (credentials plus endpoint) a Datadog Workflow Automation action uses to reach an external system -- the real, reusable authorization a workflow step calls through rather than embedding credentials per-workflow.
datadog_get_app_response: `datadog_get_app_response` is a real custom application built with Datadog App Builder -- a real, deployed internal tool (built from Datadog's own low-code components) with its own name, layout, and data connections.
datadog_get_investigation_response: `datadog_get_investigation_response` is a real Datadog Bits AI investigation -- an AI-assisted analysis session correlating an organization's own telemetry (logs, traces, metrics) around a specific incident or question, with its own findings and real, tracked state.
datadog_get_workflow_response: `datadog_get_workflow_response` is a real Datadog Workflow Automation workflow -- the actual sequence of triggers, conditions, and actions (query a system, post to Slack, create a Jira ticket) that runs automatically in response to an event.
datadog_google_chat_organization_handle_: `datadog_google_chat_organization_handle_response` is a real, configured Google Chat destination Datadog notifications can be routed to at the organization level -- the connection Datadog monitors and workflows use to post into a Google Chat space.
datadog_google_chat_target_audience_resp: `datadog_google_chat_target_audience_response` is the real, allowed audience configuration for a Google Chat integration -- which real Google Workspace domain/audience Datadog is authorized to post Chat messages to, part of Google Chat's own webhook authentication model.
datadog_historical_job_response: `datadog_historical_job_response` is a real, completed background job that computed historical data for a Datadog feature (for example, backfilling `datadog_historical_metrics_configuration_response` data) -- its own real status and time range.
datadog_historical_metrics_configuration: `datadog_historical_metrics_configuration_response` is real configuration controlling how far back, and for which metrics, Datadog computes and stores historical rollups -- used by features (like DORA metrics or degradation detection) that need trend data older than a metric's own default retention.
datadog_host_tags: `datadog_host_tags` are labels attached to one specific host that every metric, log, trace, and integration reported by that host inherits automatically. Tagging a host is what makes it possible to filter and correlate telemetry across many hosts at once, which matters most in container and cloud environments where hosts are constantly appearing and disappearing.
datadog_incident_integration_metadata_re: `datadog_incident_integration_metadata_response` is the real, linked metadata connecting a Datadog incident to an external system's own record of it -- for example, the Jira ticket or Slack channel Datadog created and is keeping in sync for that incident.
datadog_incident_notification_rule: `datadog_incident_notification_rule` is a real rule controlling when and how Datadog notifies people about an incident's own lifecycle events (declared, updated, resolved) -- who gets notified, through which channel, based on the incident's own severity or type.
datadog_incident_notification_template: `datadog_incident_notification_template` is a real, reusable message template Datadog Incident Management notifications are rendered from -- keeping incident update messages consistent in format across a team rather than hand-written each time.
datadog_incident_responder_response: `datadog_incident_responder_response` is a real person or team assigned a responder role on a Datadog incident -- who's actively working the incident, distinct from who merely has visibility into it.
datadog_incident_response: `datadog_incident_response` is v2's own richer representation of a Datadog incident -- a real, declared operational event with its own severity, timeline, responders, and postmortem, the central object Datadog Incident Management is built around.
datadog_incident_rule_response: `datadog_incident_rule_response` is a real rule that automatically classifies or acts on an incoming Datadog incident based on its own attributes -- for example, auto-assigning a severity or a responder team based on which service is affected.
datadog_incident_todo_response: `datadog_incident_todo_response` is a real, tracked action item on a Datadog incident -- a concrete follow-up task (write the postmortem, patch the root cause) with its own assignee and completion state.
datadog_incident_type_response: `datadog_incident_type_response` is a real, organization-defined category of incident (a security incident vs. an availability incident, for example) -- used to route and report on incidents differently depending on what kind of event they actually are.
datadog_incident_user_defined_field_resp: `datadog_incident_user_defined_field_response` is a real, custom field an organization adds to its own incidents beyond Datadog's built-in fields -- a way to capture org-specific data (a customer-impact tier, an internal tracking ID) on every incident.
datadog_incident_user_defined_role_respo: `datadog_incident_user_defined_role_response` is a real, custom responder role an organization defines for incidents beyond Datadog's built-in roles -- for example, "Communications Lead" or "Customer Liaison", used the same way `datadog_incident_responder_response` assigns built-in roles.
datadog_issue_response: `datadog_issue_response` is a real, tracked issue inside Datadog's issue-management surface -- a general-purpose trackable problem (used across Datadog's code-quality and security-scanning products) with its own status and assignment, distinct from a `datadog_case_response`.
datadog_jira_issue_template_response: `datadog_jira_issue_template_response` is a real, saved template controlling how Datadog creates a Jira issue when it integrates with Jira -- the real field mappings (summary, description, project, issue type) applied every time Datadog opens a Jira ticket from an incident, case, or finding.
datadog_llmobs_prompt_sdkresponse: `datadog_llmobs_prompt_sdkresponse` is a real, versioned prompt managed through Datadog LLM Observability's Prompt Hub -- letting a team track and iterate on the actual prompt text used in a production LLM application as a first-class, versioned object.
datadog_llmobs_prompt_version_response: `datadog_llmobs_prompt_version_response` is one real, saved version of a `datadog_llmobs_prompt_sdkresponse` -- the prompt's own real edit history, so a team can compare or roll back to an earlier prompt version.
datadog_logs_archive: `datadog_logs_archive` is a real, configured long-term log archive -- where Datadog forwards a copy of ingested logs (to Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage) for cheap, long-term retention and rehydration, outside Datadog's own indexed retention window.
datadog_logs_index: `datadog_logs_index` is a real Datadog log index -- a named bucket logs are routed into (by a real filter query) that controls that log traffic's own retention period and daily quota, the primary lever for controlling indexed logging cost.
datadog_logs_metric_response: `datadog_logs_metric_response` is a real, custom metric generated by aggregating log data -- letting a team turn high-volume or expensive-to-retain logs into a cheap, long-retention metric (a count or a measured value) instead of paying to index every underlying log line.
datadog_logs_pipeline: `datadog_logs_pipeline` processes incoming logs by running them through an ordered sequence of processors that parse semi-structured text into structured, named attributes. A pipeline only runs against logs matching its own filter, and the standardized attribute names it produces are what let logs from very different sources become searchable, comparable facets without changing anything on the systems producing them.
datadog_maintenance: `datadog_maintenance` is a real, scheduled maintenance window inside Datadog's Cloud Security Management -- suppresses posture/vulnerability findings for a defined scope and time range during planned, expected changes, the CSM counterpart to `datadog_downtime_response`.
datadog_maintenance_template: `datadog_maintenance_template` is a reusable template a `datadog_maintenance` window is created from -- the real, saved scope and suppression rules a team applies repeatedly rather than reconfiguring a maintenance window from scratch each time.
datadog_metric_metadata: `datadog_metric_metadata` is the description, unit, and type information attached to one specific metric, editable independently of the metric's own data points. Setting real metadata (what the metric represents, whether it's measured in bytes, requests, or seconds) is what makes a metric self-explanatory to someone who didn't define it.
datadog_microsoft_teams_tenant_based_han: `datadog_microsoft_teams_tenant_based_handle_response` is a real, configured Microsoft Teams destination tied to a connected Azure AD tenant -- the newer, tenant-based way Datadog notifications and monitors post into a Teams channel, alongside the older webhook-based handle.
datadog_microsoft_teams_workflows_webhoo: `datadog_microsoft_teams_workflows_webhook_handle_response` is a real, configured Microsoft Teams destination using a Teams Workflows (Power Automate) webhook URL -- the webhook-based way Datadog notifications post into a Teams channel, Microsoft's current replacement for the deprecated Office 365 Connector webhook.
datadog_monitor: `datadog_monitor` watches a metric, an integration's own availability, or a network endpoint against a real threshold, and alerts when it's crossed. Monitors are Datadog's own core detection mechanism -- routing notifications to the right people with the context needed to act, so problems get caught before they affect customers rather than after.
datadog_monitor_config_policy_response: `datadog_monitor_config_policy_response` is a real, org-wide policy constraining how monitors may be configured -- for example, requiring every monitor to carry a specific tag -- enforced across all monitors created in the organization, not just one.
datadog_monitor_notification_rule_respon: `datadog_monitor_notification_rule_response` is a real, centrally-managed rule controlling which real notification targets a monitor alert reaches, based on the monitor's own tags -- lets a platform team manage monitor routing centrally instead of every monitor author hand-writing its own notify list.
datadog_monitor_user_template_response: `datadog_monitor_user_template_response` is a real, saved monitor template a user or team can reuse to quickly create new monitors with consistent thresholds and messages, rather than configuring each new monitor from a blank state.
datadog_mute_rule_response: `datadog_mute_rule_response` is a real, general-purpose rule that suppresses notifications matching a condition -- used by Datadog's security products to mute recurring, already-triaged findings without disabling the underlying detection rule.
datadog_notebook_response: `datadog_notebook_response` is a collaborative document that embeds live Datadog graphs directly alongside written text, letting multiple people build an investigation, a postmortem, or a runbook together with real, current monitoring data attached to the narrative rather than screenshots that go stale.
datadog_notification_channel: `datadog_notification_channel` is a real, general-purpose configured destination for Datadog notifications -- an umbrella concept spanning the many concrete channel types (Slack, email, PagerDuty, webhook, and similar) a monitor, monitor, or workflow can notify.
datadog_notification_rule_response: `datadog_notification_rule_response` is a real, general-purpose rule controlling notification routing based on real conditions -- the general form the more specific `datadog_monitor_notification_rule_response`, `datadog_team_notification_rule_response`, and `datadog_incident_notification_rule` all specialize.
datadog_observability_pipeline: `datadog_observability_pipeline` is a real Datadog Observability Pipelines pipeline -- a configured chain of sources, processors, and destinations that shapes, filters, and routes log/telemetry data in transit, before it ever reaches Datadog's own ingestion or an external system.
datadog_okta_account_response: `datadog_okta_account_response` is a real Okta account connected to Datadog's own Okta integration -- the credentials Datadog uses to pull Okta identity and authentication events into Datadog, commonly for Cloud SIEM detection.
datadog_on_call_notification_rule: `datadog_on_call_notification_rule` is a real rule controlling how Datadog On-Call notifies a specific responder -- which device or channel (push, SMS, phone call, email) is used and in what order for that person, distinct from the team-level `datadog_escalation_policy`.
datadog_opsgenie_service_response: `datadog_opsgenie_service_response` is a real Opsgenie service connected through Datadog's Opsgenie integration -- lets a Datadog monitor page an Opsgenie service directly, for organizations running Opsgenie as their on-call tool alongside Datadog.
datadog_org_group_policy_override_respon: `datadog_org_group_policy_override_response` is a real, scoped exception to an organization-wide `datadog_org_group_policy_response` -- letting a specific org group opt out of, or customize, a policy that otherwise applies to every group by default.
datadog_org_group_policy_response: `datadog_org_group_policy_response` is a real policy applied across Datadog org groups (Datadog's multi-org/child-org structure for large enterprises) -- a governance rule enforced consistently across every child org unless a `datadog_org_group_policy_override_response` says otherwise.
datadog_org_group_response: `datadog_org_group_response` is a real group of Datadog child organizations under a parent org -- the structural unit Datadog's multi-org management features (shared policy, centralized billing visibility) operate on for enterprises running many separate Datadog orgs.
datadog_organization_response: `datadog_organization_response` represents one organization inside a real multi-org account, the deployment model Datadog itself recommends for MSPs and larger companies that need to keep each client's or team's data fully separated. A parent organization can create and view usage for child organizations without ever seeing the underlying metrics inside them, and users can be granted access to the parent, to specific children, or both.
datadog_pager_duty_service_name: `datadog_pager_duty_service_name` maps one PagerDuty service into Datadog by its own service name and integration key, which creates a real `@pagerduty-<serviceName>` notification handle. Adding that handle to a monitor's own alert text is what actually pages the right PagerDuty service when the monitor breaches, with incident severity mapped automatically from the monitor's own status.
datadog_partial_application_key_response: `datadog_partial_application_key_response` is a real, redacted view of a Datadog application key -- shows the key's own metadata (name, owner, scopes) without exposing its real secret value, the safe-to-list counterpart to the one-time-visible full `datadog_application_key_response`.
datadog_personal_access_token_response: `datadog_personal_access_token_response` is a real, user-scoped Datadog API credential -- unlike an application key (tied to a user but usable org-wide within that user's permissions), a personal access token is explicitly scoped to specific real permissions the user grants it at creation.
datadog_playlist: `datadog_playlist` is a real, ordered sequence of Datadog dashboards that auto-cycles on a timer -- commonly used to drive a real wall-mounted status display (a NOC or team room TV) through a rotating set of dashboards.
datadog_postmortem_template_response: `datadog_postmortem_template_response` is a real, reusable template a Datadog incident postmortem document is generated from -- the standard sections (timeline, root cause, action items) a team defines once and reuses for every incident writeup.
datadog_powerpack_response: `datadog_powerpack_response` is a real, reusable Datadog Powerpack -- a saved, parameterized group of dashboard widgets a team can drop onto multiple dashboards at once, keeping a common visualization (like a service's own golden signals) consistent everywhere it's used.
datadog_project_response: `datadog_project_response` is a real, tracked project inside a Datadog workflow/app-building context -- a top-level grouping (of workflows, apps, or datastores) used to organize related automation work together.
datadog_report_schedule_response: `datadog_report_schedule_response` is a real, recurring schedule for generating and delivering a Datadog report (usage, cost, or similar) automatically on a real cadence, rather than requiring someone to run it by hand each time.
datadog_restriction_policy_response: `datadog_restriction_policy_response` is a real, fine-grained access-control policy Datadog applies to a specific resource (a dashboard, a monitor, a notebook) -- who beyond the default org-role permissions may view or edit that one specific object.
datadog_restriction_query_with_relations: `datadog_restriction_query_with_relationships_response` is a real, saved logs query with restricted access, plus its own real relationships to the roles/teams permitted to use it -- lets an organization share a sensitive logs query without exposing the underlying log data to everyone.
datadog_retention_filter_response: `datadog_retention_filter_response` is v2's own general logs retention filter representation -- a real filter query that routes matching logs into a specific `datadog_logs_index` with its own retention period, the general form `datadog_rum_retention_filter_response` specializes for RUM.
datadog_role_response: `datadog_role_response` is a real Datadog organization role -- the named permission set (Datadog Admin, Standard, Read Only, or a custom role) assigned to organization members, controlling what each user is allowed to see and do.
datadog_ruleset_resp: `datadog_ruleset_resp` is a real, general-purpose named collection of detection or governance rules -- the general form behind the more specific ruleset types (`datadog_custom_ruleset_response`, `datadog_sast_ruleset_response`) elsewhere in this corpus.
datadog_rum_metric_response: `datadog_rum_metric_response` is a real, custom metric generated by aggregating Real User Monitoring (RUM) session data -- the RUM counterpart to `datadog_logs_metric_response`, turning raw session/event data into a cheap, long-retention metric.
datadog_rum_retention_filter_response: `datadog_rum_retention_filter_response` is a real filter controlling which RUM sessions Datadog actually retains in full -- since RUM data volume can be very high, this filter decides which sessions (by real criteria like error presence or a specific user segment) are worth keeping versus sampling out.
datadog_rum_retention_quota_config_respo: `datadog_rum_retention_quota_config_response` is the real, configured quota (a percentage or a hard cap) for how much RUM session volume a `datadog_rum_retention_filter_response` is allowed to retain -- controls the actual cost impact of a retention filter.
datadog_rum_sdk_config_response: `datadog_rum_sdk_config_response` is real, centrally-managed configuration for the Datadog RUM browser/mobile SDK -- letting a team control SDK behavior (sampling rates, feature flags) for a RUM application from Datadog itself rather than only through code-level SDK init options.
datadog_rumapplication_response: `datadog_rumapplication_response` is a real Datadog RUM application -- the top-level object representing one real monitored web or mobile application, identified by its own real RUM application ID and client token.
datadog_rumoperation_response: `datadog_rumoperation_response` is a real, named RUM operation -- a specific real user-facing interaction or view Datadog RUM tracks performance for (matching by name), distinct from the app-level `datadog_rumapplication_response`.
datadog_sast_ruleset_response: `datadog_sast_ruleset_response` is a real, named collection of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) rules -- the ruleset used to scan source code for real vulnerability patterns as part of Datadog Code Security.
datadog_scan_result_response: `datadog_scan_result_response` is a real, individual result produced by one of Datadog's security scans (a code, cloud posture, or vulnerability scan) -- the actual finding, before it's necessarily promoted into a tracked `datadog_case_response` or `datadog_issue_response`.
datadog_schedule: `datadog_schedule` is a real Datadog On-Call schedule -- who is on-call and when, the rotation Datadog's escalation policies actually page against.
datadog_secure_embed_get_response: `datadog_secure_embed_get_response` is a real, secure, shareable embed of a Datadog dashboard or graph -- a signed, access-controlled URL a team can embed in an external page or status site without exposing that dashboard to the public internet unrestricted.
datadog_security_filter_response: `datadog_security_filter_response` is a real filter controlling which logs are actually evaluated by Datadog Cloud SIEM's security-monitoring detection rules -- scoping detection to relevant log traffic and excluding known-noisy or irrelevant sources.
datadog_security_monitoring_critical_ass: `datadog_security_monitoring_critical_asset_response` is a real asset an organization has flagged as business-critical inside Datadog Cloud SIEM -- security findings touching a critical asset are weighted/prioritized differently than the same finding on a non-critical one.
datadog_security_monitoring_dataset_resp: `datadog_security_monitoring_dataset_response` is a real, defined dataset scoped specifically for Cloud SIEM security-monitoring rules to run against -- the security-specific counterpart to the general `datadog_dataset_response_single`.
datadog_security_monitoring_integration_: `datadog_security_monitoring_integration_config_response` is real configuration controlling how a specific third-party integration's data feeds into Datadog Cloud SIEM's own detection rules.
datadog_security_monitoring_suppression_: `datadog_security_monitoring_suppression_response` is a real, scoped rule that suppresses a Cloud SIEM security signal matching real criteria (already investigated, known false positive) without disabling the underlying detection rule for everyone else.
datadog_security_monitoring_suppressions: `datadog_security_monitoring_suppressions_response` is the real, listable collection view over an organization's configured `datadog_security_monitoring_suppression_response` entries.
datadog_security_monitoring_terraform_ex: `datadog_security_monitoring_terraform_export_response` is a real, generated Terraform representation of an organization's own Cloud SIEM detection rule configuration -- lets a team export their live security-monitoring setup as real, reviewable infrastructure-as-code.
datadog_service_access_token_response: `datadog_service_access_token_response` is a real credential scoped to a specific service (not a human user) -- used by Datadog's Software Catalog / service-to-service auth surface for machine access rather than a `datadog_personal_access_token_response`.
datadog_service_definition_get_response: `datadog_service_definition_get_response` is a real Datadog Software Catalog service definition -- the real, structured metadata (owning team, repository, on-call, documentation links) describing one service, the object Software Catalog is built on.
datadog_service_now_template_response: `datadog_service_now_template_response` is a real, saved template controlling how Datadog creates a ServiceNow ticket when it integrates with ServiceNow -- the ServiceNow counterpart to `datadog_jira_issue_template_response`.
datadog_severity_modifier_rule_response: `datadog_severity_modifier_rule_response` is a real rule that adjusts a security finding's or incident's severity based on real context (a critical asset, a specific environment) -- lets an organization's own risk context override a detection's default severity.
datadog_shared_dashboard: `datadog_shared_dashboard` publishes a dashboard to a public link that anyone can view outside Datadog entirely, without a Datadog account or credentials. It's the mechanism for showing metric, trace, and log visualizations to people outside your organization, and every publicly shared dashboard can be tracked and revoked from one place in your account settings.
datadog_slack_integration_channel: `datadog_slack_integration_channel` connects one Slack channel to Datadog so monitor alerts and other notifications can post into it -- set up by inviting the Datadog app into the channel with `/invite @Datadog`, after which the channel becomes a real, addressable notification target and can also run `/datadog` commands directly from Slack.
datadog_slocorrection_response: `datadog_slocorrection_response` excludes a specific time window -- one-time or recurring -- from an SLO's own error-budget calculation. It's the real mechanism for making sure a scheduled maintenance window or a planned deployment doesn't unfairly count against reliability targets that were never meant to cover it.
datadog_sloresponse: `datadog_sloresponse` defines a quantified target for how reliably a service should perform over a given time window. SLOs give a team a concrete, shared number to balance new feature work against platform stability, and to communicate reliability honestly with people outside the team who depend on the service.
datadog_spans_metric_response: `datadog_spans_metric_response` is a real, custom metric generated by aggregating APM span data -- the tracing counterpart to `datadog_logs_metric_response`/`datadog_rum_metric_response`, turning high-cardinality span data into a cheap, long-retention metric.
datadog_status_page: `datadog_status_page` is a real, public or private Datadog Status Page -- a real, hosted status/incident-communication page an organization publishes to communicate service health to its own customers or internal stakeholders.
datadog_status_pages_component: `datadog_status_pages_component` is a real, individual component (a listed service or subsystem) shown on a `datadog_status_page`, each with its own real, independently reported status.
datadog_synthetics_apitest: `datadog_synthetics_apitest` sends real requests against a system's own network layers -- HTTP, SSL, DNS, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, ICMP, or gRPC -- from managed or private locations, to catch degraded performance or an unexpected response before a real user does. A failing test can alert a team, block a CI pipeline, or trigger a rollback directly.
datadog_synthetics_browser_test: `datadog_synthetics_browser_test` runs a scripted user journey through a real application on a schedule, from multiple real locations, browsers, and devices, to confirm both that the app is reachable and that a specific real user flow still actually works end to end.
datadog_synthetics_downtime_response: `datadog_synthetics_downtime_response` is a real, scheduled suppression window specifically for Synthetic Monitoring tests -- mutes synthetic test alerts during planned maintenance, the Synthetics-scoped counterpart to `datadog_downtime_response`.
datadog_synthetics_global_variable: `datadog_synthetics_global_variable` is a value shared across every Synthetic test in an organization, rather than duplicated inside each one -- used for things like an auth token pulled from a prior API response or a generated UUID, so tests stay dynamic instead of hardcoding values that go stale.
datadog_synthetics_mobile_test: `datadog_synthetics_mobile_test` runs a predefined workflow against a real Android or iOS app on real physical devices, capturing a screenshot and a pass/fail result at every step. Tests can run on a schedule, on demand, or as part of a CI/CD pipeline, to catch mobile-specific regressions before real users hit them.
datadog_synthetics_network_test_response: `datadog_synthetics_network_test_response` is a real Datadog Synthetic Monitoring network test -- checks real TCP/UDP/ICMP-level connectivity and performance to an endpoint, distinct from an HTTP-level API test or a browser test.
datadog_synthetics_private_location: `datadog_synthetics_private_location` is a Docker container or Windows service you run inside your own network so Synthetic tests can reach internal endpoints that the public internet, and Datadog's own managed test locations, can't. It's the real option for testing anything behind a firewall, including internal CI environments before a release ever reaches production.
datadog_synthetics_suite_response: `datadog_synthetics_suite_response` is a real, named group of Synthetic Monitoring tests run and reported on together -- lets a team organize related synthetic checks (all the tests for one user journey, for example) as one unit.
datadog_table_result_v2: `datadog_table_result_v2` is a real, structured tabular result produced by a Datadog query or workflow step -- rows and columns of real data, the shape used when a Datadog feature needs to hand back tabular output rather than a single value or time series.
datadog_tag_indexing_rule_response: `datadog_tag_indexing_rule_response` is a real rule controlling which tag keys Datadog actually indexes for fast filtering/faceting -- since indexing every possible tag isn't free at scale, this rule is how an organization controls which tags stay queryable.
datadog_tag_policy_response: `datadog_tag_policy_response` is a real, org-wide policy enforcing tag governance -- for example, requiring a specific tag key to be present, or restricting a tag's allowed values, applied consistently across the resources it's scoped to.
datadog_team_hierarchy_link_response: `datadog_team_hierarchy_link_response` is a real, structural link expressing that one Datadog Team is a sub-team of another -- the mechanism Datadog Teams uses to model a real organizational hierarchy rather than a flat list of unrelated teams.
datadog_team_link_response: `datadog_team_link_response` is a real, external link attached to a Datadog Team -- a quick-reference URL (to a runbook, a repo, a dashboard) the team keeps associated with itself for others to find easily.
datadog_team_notification_rule_response: `datadog_team_notification_rule_response` is a real rule controlling how a specific Datadog Team is notified -- which channel that team's own alerts route to, scoped to the team rather than to a single monitor.
datadog_team_response: `datadog_team_response` is v2's own richer representation of a Datadog Team -- a real, named group of users used across Datadog (ownership on services, routing for notifications, on-call) as the organizing unit smaller than the whole org.
datadog_tenancy_config: `datadog_tenancy_config` is real, org-level configuration controlling Datadog's own multi-tenancy behavior for an organization -- part of the underlying structure that `datadog_org_group_response` and related multi-org features are built on.
datadog_ticket_creation_rule_response: `datadog_ticket_creation_rule_response` is a real rule that automatically creates an external ticket (Jira, ServiceNow) when a real condition is met -- for example, automatically opening a Jira ticket the moment a Datadog incident is declared, using the linked `datadog_jira_issue_template_response`.
datadog_ucconfig_pair: `datadog_ucconfig_pair` is a real, paired configuration entry inside Datadog Cloud Cost Management's usage-and-cost (UC) configuration -- one real key/value association (for example, mapping a cloud account to a cost-attribution tag) the cost pipeline uses.
datadog_user_invitation_response: `datadog_user_invitation_response` is a real, pending invitation for someone to join a Datadog organization -- the invited email, the role they'll be granted, and the invitation's own real status until it's accepted.
datadog_user_response: `datadog_user_response` represents one person's account inside a Datadog organization, along with the roles and permissions that determine what they can actually do -- managed from the Users tab in Organization Settings, where an admin invites, assigns roles to, and can disable individual accounts.
datadog_v2_event_response: `datadog_v2_event_response` is v2's own richer representation of a Datadog Event -- a real, timestamped occurrence (a deploy, an alert, a comment) posted to the Event stream, distinct from this same resource's plain `datadog_event_response` (v1) by carrying a real, structured `attributes` payload instead of v1's flatter shape.
datadog_web_integration_account_response: `datadog_web_integration_account_response` is a real, connected account for one of Datadog's simpler, credential-based web integrations -- the general shape behind an integration that only needs an account identifier and a secret, rather than a full OAuth flow.
datadog_webhooks_integration: `datadog_webhooks_integration` sends a real POST request to an external endpoint whenever a monitor alert fires, triggered by adding `@webhook-<name>` to the monitor's own alert text. Built-in variables like `$ALERT_ID` and `$ALERT_STATUS` populate the payload automatically, giving the receiving service real, structured context about exactly what happened.
datadog_webhooks_integration_custom_vari: `datadog_webhooks_integration_custom_variable_response` is a named value you define once in the webhooks integration tile and then reuse across a webhook's own URL, payload, or headers -- useful for a credential or another value several webhook configurations all need but that shouldn't be hardcoded into each one separately.
datadog_webhooks_oauth2_client_credentia: `datadog_webhooks_oauth2_client_credentials_response` is real, configured OAuth2 client-credentials authentication for a Datadog outbound webhook -- lets a webhook integration authenticate to the receiving system using OAuth2 client credentials instead of a static secret.
datadog_widget_response: `datadog_widget_response` is a real, standalone Datadog dashboard widget -- one real visualization (a timeseries graph, a query value, a table) addressable on its own, outside the context of the full dashboard it may also appear on.
datadog_worklflow_get_instance_response: `datadog_worklflow_get_instance_response` is a real, running or completed instance of a Datadog Workflow Automation workflow -- one real execution of a `datadog_get_workflow_response` definition, with its own real status and step-by-step results (the misspelled "worklflow" reflects Datadog's own real, live wire name, not a transcription error here).
